items.summary: IRGC claims attack on US radar system in Bahrain, as Manama says it thwarted them Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said that it carried out a drone attack targeting a US radar system at the Isa airbase in Bahrain. items.title: Iran launches attacks on military base in Kuwait
items.summary: Iran launches attacks on military base in Kuwait Submitted by MEE staff on Wed, 11/18/2026 - 09:34 The Iranian army said it had targeted the Ali al-Salem Airbase in Kuwait, while the cause of a building fire in Bahrain is being investigated Missiles are put on display in central Tehran on 28 September (AFP) Off Iran has launched a series of attacks against its Gulf neighbours in Kuwait and Bahrain , as tensions continue to simmer. In a statement published on state media early on Wednesday, the Iranian army said it fired a drone targeting the Ali al-Salem Airbase in Kuwait. "This morning, the Islamic Republic of Iran's army's destructive combat drones targeted Patriot defense systems and drone and missile launchers of the US terrorist army at the Ali al-Salem base in Kuwait with destructive drones," the statement read. "In defense of Iran, we will not bow to any power, but our response to any threat or aggression will be decisive, crushing, and without geographical limitations," the army added Earlier, the Kuwaiti ⁠⁠military said ⁠⁠that its air defences were ⁠⁠countering the ⁠⁠attack.

items.title: Kuwait slams Iranian attacks on its territory
items.summary: Kuwait slams Iranian attacks on its territory Kuwait’s foreign ministry has condemned the latest Iranian drone attack on its territory. The ministry denounced the attacks as "repeated and criminal" and described it as a "direct threat" to the Gulf country's "security and stability". "The Ministry reaffirms that the continuation of these attacks constitutes a dangerous escalation that threatens the region’s security and stability and undermines diplomatic efforts aimed at de-escalation and reducing tensions," the ministry said in its statement posted on X. It added that Kuwait retains the right to "take all necessary measures to safeguard its sovereignty, preserve its security and defend its territory and vital facilities against any aggression or threat, in exercise of its inherent right to self-defence".

clusters.headline: China issues 'peace declaration' agreed with Trump and Putin

items.title: China issues 'peace declaration' agreed with Trump and Putin
items.summary: China issues 'peace declaration' agreed with Trump and Putin China has released a “peace declaration” it said its President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin had agreed on at their unprecedented three-way meeting, where they said nuclear wars were futile and should never be fought. All three countries committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security, according to a four-point declaration published by Chinese official media Xinhua. The leaders reportedly discussed Russia's war in Ukraine and the US-Israeli war on Iran. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons, Xinhua said. The three heads of state also agreed on reform for a "more effective" United Nations, and said that the International Criminal Court and similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction, according to the declaration.

items.summary: Trump lands in China for meeting with Xi and Putin US President Donald Trump has arrived in China for the Apec summit in Shenzhen, where he is expected to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladmir Putin. The historic trilateral meeting between the leaders will take place on Thursday. Xi, Trump and Putin are due to meet on the sidelines of the summit to potentially discuss Russia's war with Ukraine and the US-Israeli war on Iran, as well as trade, AI and nuclear weapons. Xi met Trump off the plane on the tarmac at Shenzhen, reciprocating Trump's gesture when the Chinese leader visited the US in September. Xi told Trump he hoped their talks would help advance a “constructive, strategic and stable relationship” between China and the US, based on “respect, fairness and reciprocity”, according to China’s state news agency Xinhua. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that Putin and Trump are unlikely to have time for fully fledged bilateral negotiations in China, but may talk on the event's sidelines, the Tass news agency reported. items.summary: Saudi finance minister claims kingdom can withstand prolonged Houthi conflict Saudi Finance Minister Mohammed al-Jadaan says the kingdom is “resilient enough to withstand a prolonged conflict” with Yemen’s Houthis. Speaking to reporters, al-Jadaan dismissed as “a total mistake” any expectation that attacks on civilian infrastructure or “blackmail by missiles” would force Riyadh to compromise its national security. He said Saudi Arabia plans to reduce its budget deficit to 3.6 percent of GDP in 2027, compared with an estimated 4.9 percent this year, despite the escalating fighting. The Iran-backed Houthis say their missile and drone campaign aims to force Riyadh to withdraw support for Yemen’s government. Al-Jadaan said reduced oil production had driven a 2.1 percent contraction in Saudi GDP this year.

Yet here he was, courting partners in Samarkand, a city that epitomizes the historic Persianate realm , whose inhabitants still predominantly speak Tajik , a variant of Persian. The irony was not lost on Iranian diplomats, who took to social media to troll Rubio over the incongruity. The American-Uzbek Business & Investment Council announced 54 deals worth $12 billion as a result of the visit. items.summary: US intelligence, homeland security chiefs clash over Iranian 'dirty bomb' reports US director of national intelligence Jay Clayton echoed warnings on Wednesday that Washington faces "a heightened threat from Iranians' lethal plotting against our citizens at home and abroad," in response to a question regarding reports of an alleged Iranian plot to detonate a so-called "dirty bomb" in the US. However, US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin contradicted the statement, saying on Wednesday that he does not believe that Iran poses an immediate threat to the US with the dirty bomb plot. This comes after Secretary of State Marco Rubio also dismissed the CNN report, citing US intelligence, which claimed Iran was developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials with a chemical weapon.

clusters.headline: Are US aircraft carriers becoming $22 billion liabilities?

items.title: Are US aircraft carriers becoming $22 billion liabilities?
items.summary: The Bunker appears originally at the Project on Government Oversight and is republished here with permission. Armchair admirals like to quote presidents demanding to know “where are the carriers?” when trouble erupts somewhere around the world. That’s why there was a wave of stories last week when the U.S. carrier presence near Iran jumped from two to three. It was “a dramatic show of military might as President Donald Trump keeps his options open for next steps in the Iran war,” the Associated Press reported November 16. Two days later, when one of the carriers left the region, not so much. What had been a “dramatic show of military might” on Monday turned into a mere “shuffling of aircraft carriers in the Middle East” by Wednesday, the AP said . Such high-seas tracking should come as no surprise. Crow’s nests and watchstanders have been replaced by satellites and websites . There are even websites dedicated to locating the U.S. Navy’s 11 aircraft carriers. items.title: UK moving military planes into hangars amid drone threat: Reports
items.summary: UK moving military planes into hangars amid drone threat: Reports Britain's air force is moving planes into hangars and hardened shelters overnight to protect them from drone threats, The Times and Sky News reported on Wednesday. The two UK media outlets also revealed plans by the Royal Air Force (RAF) to install anti-drone nets around warplanes that remain exposed. The Ministry of Defence did not confirm the reports, but in a statement to AFP said it takes "the security of our bases, equipment and personnel very seriously and (is) always adapting to counter any potential threats". The ministry said it was "investing an additional £470 million ($615 million) to strengthen security at military sites, including better physical protection, surveillance and counter-drone capabilities". British authorities have regularly issued warnings about the threats posed by Russia and Iran and the government has urged the country to be prepared for different contingencies.

An ethnography from Adygea traces the scalar negotiation of Circassian and Russian and grassroots rescaling efforts. A study of Uzbek symbolism shows a shared language linking textile ornament and Timurid architecture as living heritage. Each piece, in our view, offers the reader something new not only in its content but also in its research approach.

items.title: Milieuramp in Straat van Hormuz: 'Effecten olievervuiling over veertig jaar nog zichtbaar'
items.summary: De oorlog tussen de Verenigde Staten en Iran eist niet alleen een zware menselijke en economische tol, maar veroorzaakt ook een groeiende milieuramp. Satellietbeelden laten honderden olievervuilingen zien in de Straat van Hormuz en de Perzische Golf. Terwijl betrokken landen dit stilhouden, waarschuwen internationale wetenschappers dat de schade aan kwetsbare ecosystemen nog tientallen jaren zichtbaar kan zijn. Vanuit de ruimte zijn ze duidelijk te zien: grote, donkere olievlekken die zich over het water verspreiden. Sinds het uitbreken van de oorlog zijn olietankers herhaaldelijk getroffen door raketten, explosies en zeemijnen. Daarbij zijn grote hoeveelheden ruwe olie en stookolie in zee terechtgekomen. Volgens Greenpeace zijn op basis van satellietwaarnemingen inmiddels meer dan 600 mogelijke olievlekken geregistreerd: in de Perzische Golf, de Straat van Hormuz en de Arabische Zee. Bij elkaar opgeteld beslaan ze ongeveer 21.000 vierkante kilometer, een gebied groter dan Slovenië. Hoe groot de schade precies is, is op dit moment moeilijk vast te stellen. items.title: The best thing I ever ate? Lunch on the strait of Hormuz
items.summary: The idea of any guest being hungry, or there not being enough food, is an unspeakable proposition for an Iranian host When most people think of the strait of Hormuz, the warm, tropical waterway connecting the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman, incredible food isn’t usually the first thing that comes to mind. But it should be, and I would know – it’s where I had one of my most memorable meals. I was visiting Iran, traversing thousands of miles across the country with a local female photographer, mapping out regional specialities for my cookbook The Saffron Tales . Over the course of several months, we cooked and ate in people’s home kitchens, meeting a cross-section of society, from farmers and pharmacists to yoga teachers and restaurant owners, who all shared their favourite foods with us in places as diverse as the snowy mountains outside Tabriz, the rice paddies of the Caspian Sea, and the historic cities of Isfahan and Shiraz. The Saffron Tales: Recipes and Stories from the Persian Kitchen by Yasmin Khan, published by Bloomsbury at £26. To order a copy for £23.40, go to guardianbo

Speaking to Turkish broadcaster TGRT Haber on Saturday, Fidan warned that the fallout from the conflict is threatening international markets. “It is heading toward having very destructive effects,” he said. Fidan said diplomatic efforts to re-open the Strait of Hormuz remain active, even though the process appears to be deadlocked, citing his recent discussion with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani. He also said that Ankara was keeping the humanitarian crisis in Gaza on the global radar permanently despite other international crises. "In every speech, every initiative, and every platform wherever it may be, the Gaza issue is one we have not, and will not, allow to be forgotten," Fidan said.

items.summary: UKMTO weekly report says six vessels attacked in and around Hormuz The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) has said six attacks on commercial vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz were reported in the past week, while shipping traffic remained about 65 percent below pre-war levels. In its weekly report published on Friday, UKMTO said four of the six incidents occurred in the Strait of Hormuz and two in the Arabian Gulf. The UKMTO recorded 115 outbound and 148 inbound transits during the seven days to November 18, including US-facilitated movements. The combined figure was down from 139 outbound and 169 inbound the previous week. Around half of Strait of Hormuz transits involved energy carriers. Most vessels broadcasting AIS continued to use the Iranian route, although UKMTO noted an increase in traffic along the southern route. No attacks were recorded in the past week in the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandab, with the last confirmed attack recorded on August 24. items.title: Trump envoys met Qatari officials in Berlin to discuss US-Iran mediation, report says
items.summary: Trump envoys met Qatari officials in Berlin to discuss US-Iran mediation, report says US President Donald Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met senior Qatari officials in Berlin on Thursday to discuss mediation efforts between the US and Iran , Axios reported on Friday, citing two sources with knowledge of the meeting. The meeting came as Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani was in Germany on a visit. Following talks with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Berlin, the emir called for diplomatic efforts to de-escalate conflicts across the Middle East. On the sidelines of the visit, Qatari Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani met his German counterpart Johann Wadephul. The two discussed ongoing diplomatic efforts and joint coordination to de-escalate tensions and enhance security and stability in the region, according to the Qatari foreign ministry.

items.summary: Trump says US will find out about Iranian dirty bomb plot 'rumour' US President Donald Trump said on Friday that there was a "rumour" that Iran was building a dirty bomb. He added that if Iran was doing so, the United States would find out and stop it. CNN had reported earlier this week that US intelligence indicated Iran could be attempting to build a dirty bomb and detonate it in Washington. Iran's foreign ministry denied the allegations on Tuesday, calling them "baseless". A dirty bomb is far less destructive than a nuclear bomb, which relies on a fission reaction. Speaking to reporters, Trump also repeated his claim that the US has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz. "Last week, we took out record amounts of oil from the Hormuz Strait. Our navy has a blockade," he said. "We have total control over the Hormuz Strait." "Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, ever," he added. US President Donald Trump points as reporters raise their hands to ask questions during a press conference at the White House in Washington, DC, 20 November 2026 (REUTERS/Kylie Cooper)

items.title: What Ukraine Hath Wrought: Lessons for War, If We’re Listening
items.summary: Four years into Russia’s war against Ukraine, what should the U.S. military have learned by now? Michael Kofman (Carnegie Endowment), Dara Massicot (Carnegie Endowment), and Amos Fox (Arizona State University) join Ryan to discuss. The easy answer is drones and AI, but our guests argue the harder truths lie elsewhere: “Old-fashioned” ideas like campaigning, holding territory, mass, and attrition still decide wars. And, as they discuss, based on U.S. performance in the war with Iran, it may be that not much learning has happened at all.Image: ArmyInform The post What Ukraine Hath Wrought: Lessons for War, If We’re Listening appeared first on War on the Rocks .

items.title: Tanker catches fire after projectile strike near Strait of Hormuz - UKMTO
items.summary: Tanker catches fire after projectile strike near Strait of Hormuz - UKMTO A tanker caught fire after a projectile struck it while sailing through the Strait of Hormuz, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency said on Friday. The incident occurred 8 nautical miles north of the Omani town of Khasab, UKMTO said, adding that no casualties or environmental impact were reported. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said shortly afterwards that an oil tanker had caught fire after hitting a mine while attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz near Khasab, Iranian media reported. Khasab is located on Oman's Musandam Peninsula at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: US must leave West Asia and return to its own region, Iranian lawmaker says
items.summary: US must leave West Asia and return to its own region, Iranian lawmaker says An Iranian lawmaker said the United States must withdraw from West Asia and return to its own geographic sphere. Major-General Mohammad Esmaeil Kowsari, a member of parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, told Iran’s Mehr news agency that the US could no longer confront Iran. Kowsari also pointed to US threats against Iran’s nuclear programme and proposals for an economic, land, air and naval blockade of the country. items.title: Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper hit in Houthi strike on Saudi wealth fund HQ
items.summary: By Timour Azhari RIYADH, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Riyadh's tallest skyscraper, headquarters of the Saudi sovereign wealth fund, was struck on Thursday by a suspected Houthi missile in the latest blow in the Iran-backed Yemeni group's war with the kingdom. The strike blew out windows across seven to eight floors of PIF Tower, bending parts of its metal facade. It was the second time in less than two weeks that a Houthi attack damaged a landmark in Riyadh's financial district, with state oil giant Aramco's building hit in a November 8 attack.

"De energiesector en de wereldeconomie hebben dan wel weerbaarheid laten zien. Maar hoe langer de crisis duurt, hoe dieper deze zijn sporen nalaat. Ik zie geen geloofwaardige manier waarop de energiewereld teruggaat naar hoe het hiervoor was." Het agentschap doet niet één toekomstvoorspelling, maar schetst verschillende scenario's van hoe de energiewereld zich zal ontwikkelen. In comments carried by Iran's Fars News Agency, the IRGC's navy said that one of the ships was a supertanker carrying over 2m barrels of crude oil, while the other was transporting liquefied natural gas. It added that both vessels, which it said were supported by US forces, had breached Iran's protocol for crossing the contested waterway.

items.title: Tom Friedman’s deceptive effort to lure Dems to escalate in Iran
items.summary: The centrist Democrats’ campaign to rescue - not end - Donald Trump’s illegal war with Iran has officially begun. Behold Tom Friedman’s column today in The New York Times. Tom puts forward an argument with a clever structure. He starts by blasting Trump’s decision to start the war. items.title: Trump-Xi-Putin meet could be more important than you think
items.summary: The trilateral summit scheduled between President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping should be seen as the first tentative step towards — ideally — a “concert of powers” in which the leading states of the world will manage relations between themselves in such a way as to preserve and promote international peace. In this way, even if the meeting — which is supposed to take place Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit — leads to no concrete results, it will still be worth doing. Le immagini sono accompagnate da un messaggio dedicato alle vittime dell'attacco, che gli Stati Uniti attribuiscono a Hezbollah e all'Iran.L'attentato del 1983, avvenuto durante la guerra civile libanese, provocò la morte di 220 Marines, 18 marinai della Marina e tre soldati dell'Esercito americano.

items.title: Are US aircraft carriers becoming $22 billion liabilities?
items.summary: The Bunker appears originally at the Project on Government Oversight and is republished here with permission. Armchair admirals like to quote presidents demanding to know “where are the carriers?” when trouble erupts somewhere around the world. That’s why there was a wave of stories last week when the U.S. carrier presence near Iran jumped from two to three. It was “a dramatic show of military might as President Donald Trump keeps his options open for next steps in the Iran war,” the Associated Press reported November 16. Two days later, when one of the carriers left the region, not so much. What had been a “dramatic show of military might” on Monday turned into a mere “shuffling of aircraft carriers in the Middle East” by Wednesday, the AP said . Such high-seas tracking should come as no surprise. Crow’s nests and watchstanders have been replaced by satellites and websites . There are even websites dedicated to locating the U.S. Navy’s 11 aircraft carriers. items.title: Democratic voters want Congress to cut funding for Iran war: polls
items.summary: Democratic voters want Congress to quickly cut off funding for the Iran war and are prepared to punish lawmakers who fail to do so, two new polls suggest. With government funding set to expire on December 11, congressional Democrats are weighing whether to withhold their support for any spending bill unless it includes restrictions on funding for the war. Such a move would leave Trump and congressional supporters of the conflict to decide whether to accept those restrictions or risk a government shutdown to keep the war going. The new polling indicates that pursuing this strategy would have considerable support among the Democratic party’s base. Opposition to the Iran war helped fuel Democrats’ sweeping midterm victories earlier this month. Now, the question of how quickly the party should move to end the conflict has become a dividing line for the party, including in the race for Senate majority leader. Sen. items.title: UK moving military planes into hangars amid drone threat: Reports
items.summary: UK moving military planes into hangars amid drone threat: Reports Britain's air force is moving planes into hangars and hardened shelters overnight to protect them from drone threats, The Times and Sky News reported on Wednesday. The two UK media outlets also revealed plans by the Royal Air Force (RAF) to install anti-drone nets around warplanes that remain exposed. The Ministry of Defence did not confirm the reports, but in a statement to AFP said it takes "the security of our bases, equipment and personnel very seriously and (is) always adapting to counter any potential threats". The ministry said it was "investing an additional £470 million ($615 million) to strengthen security at military sites, including better physical protection, surveillance and counter-drone capabilities". British authorities have regularly issued warnings about the threats posed by Russia and Iran and the government has urged the country to be prepared for different contingencies.

items.title: Monthly Monitoring of Analytical Publications on Post-Soviet Conflicts
items.summary: This issue unites five studies. Research on Georgia reveals how youth educational aspirations shape labour emigration, remittance economies and brain drain. A 2026 EMNLP paper presents HistoricalMisinfo (500 contested events from 45 regions) and audits LLMs, finding revisionism mainly through omission and false balance. A Frontiers in Public Health editorial reads COVID-19 as a stress test for Semashko legacies, public-private coordination, burnout and inequalities. An ethnography from Adygea traces the scalar negotiation of Circassian and Russian and grassroots rescaling efforts. A study of Uzbek symbolism shows a shared language linking textile ornament and Timurid architecture as living heritage. Each piece, in our view, offers the reader something new not only in its content but also in its research approach.

Just a few days earlier in Athens, Greece, Rubio had spoken against ancient Persia as an invader and destroyer in a speech purportedly extolling Western civilization. Yet here he was, courting partners in Samarkand, a city that epitomizes the historic Persianate realm , whose inhabitants still predominantly speak Tajik , a variant of Persian. The American-Uzbek Business & Investment Council announced 54 deals worth $12 billion as a result of the visit. items.summary: Last week the leaders of the Quad (Quadrilateral Security Dialogue )— comprised of Australia, India, Japan, and the United States — met in the Philippines for the first time in two years. President Donald Trump was in Manila for less than 24 hours with a jam-packed schedule, including his participation in the main event, which was the ASEAN Summit, as well as a bilateral engagement with President Ferdinand Marcos and the Quad summit itself. Perhaps because of this busy itinerary, the Quad was given extremely short shrift, with Trump scheduled to participate for a mere 55 minutes total. But that was only part of the problem. Since the Quad’s last summit in 2024 during President Joe Biden’s administration, the strategic bloc’s members have grown increasingly frustrated with the lack of formal meetings. India is particularly aggrieved because Trump refused to travel to New Delhi when it hosted the Quad last year. items.title: Saudi finance minister claims kingdom can withstand prolonged Houthi conflict
items.summary: Saudi finance minister claims kingdom can withstand prolonged Houthi conflict Saudi Finance Minister Mohammed al-Jadaan says the kingdom is “resilient enough to withstand a prolonged conflict” with Yemen’s Houthis. Speaking to reporters, al-Jadaan dismissed as “a total mistake” any expectation that attacks on civilian infrastructure or “blackmail by missiles” would force Riyadh to compromise its national security. He said Saudi Arabia plans to reduce its budget deficit to 3.6 percent of GDP in 2027, compared with an estimated 4.9 percent this year, despite the escalating fighting. The Iran-backed Houthis say their missile and drone campaign aims to force Riyadh to withdraw support for Yemen’s government. Al-Jadaan said reduced oil production had driven a 2.1 percent contraction in Saudi GDP this year.

items.title: US eyes Iran as possible culprit in dozens of new cyberattacks against ships, WSJ reports

items.title: Milieuramp in Straat van Hormuz: 'Effecten olievervuiling over veertig jaar nog zichtbaar'
items.summary: De oorlog tussen de Verenigde Staten en Iran eist niet alleen een zware menselijke en economische tol, maar veroorzaakt ook een groeiende milieuramp. Satellietbeelden laten honderden olievervuilingen zien in de Straat van Hormuz en de Perzische Golf. Terwijl betrokken landen dit stilhouden, waarschuwen internationale wetenschappers dat de schade aan kwetsbare ecosystemen nog tientallen jaren zichtbaar kan zijn. Vanuit de ruimte zijn ze duidelijk te zien: grote, donkere olievlekken die zich over het water verspreiden. Sinds het uitbreken van de oorlog zijn olietankers herhaaldelijk getroffen door raketten, explosies en zeemijnen. Daarbij zijn grote hoeveelheden ruwe olie en stookolie in zee terechtgekomen. Volgens Greenpeace zijn op basis van satellietwaarnemingen inmiddels meer dan 600 mogelijke olievlekken geregistreerd: in de Perzische Golf, de Straat van Hormuz en de Arabische Zee. Bij elkaar opgeteld beslaan ze ongeveer 21.000 vierkante kilometer, een gebied groter dan Slovenië. Hoe groot de schade precies is, is op dit moment moeilijk vast te stellen. According to the Fars news agency, the navy said the tankers had switched off their detection and navigation systems and struck the mines north of Ghanam Island. Both vessels reportedly stopped moving. Supertankers usually carry two million barrels of oil or more, about twice as much as a standard tanker. The navy also warned that relying on "smugglers such as CENTCOM", referring to US Central Command, would result in "nothing but heavy losses". UK Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) also said on Sunday it had received a report of an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman. It gave no further details, saying only that authorities were aware and an investigation was under way. It was unclear whether the incident involved either of the tankers Iran described. items.title: The best thing I ever ate? Lunch on the strait of Hormuz
items.summary: The idea of any guest being hungry, or there not being enough food, is an unspeakable proposition for an Iranian host When most people think of the strait of Hormuz, the warm, tropical waterway connecting the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman, incredible food isn’t usually the first thing that comes to mind. But it should be, and I would know – it’s where I had one of my most memorable meals. I was visiting Iran, traversing thousands of miles across the country with a local female photographer, mapping out regional specialities for my cookbook The Saffron Tales . Over the course of several months, we cooked and ate in people’s home kitchens, meeting a cross-section of society, from farmers and pharmacists to yoga teachers and restaurant owners, who all shared their favourite foods with us in places as diverse as the snowy mountains outside Tabriz, the rice paddies of the Caspian Sea, and the historic cities of Isfahan and Shiraz. items.title: UKMTO weekly report says six vessels attacked in and around Hormuz
items.summary: UKMTO weekly report says six vessels attacked in and around Hormuz The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) has said six attacks on commercial vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz were reported in the past week, while shipping traffic remained about 65 percent below pre-war levels. In its weekly report published on Friday, UKMTO said four of the six incidents occurred in the Strait of Hormuz and two in the Arabian Gulf. The UKMTO recorded 115 outbound and 148 inbound transits during the seven days to November 18, including US-facilitated movements. The combined figure was down from 139 outbound and 169 inbound the previous week. Around half of Strait of Hormuz transits involved energy carriers. Most vessels broadcasting AIS continued to use the Iranian route, although UKMTO noted an increase in traffic along the southern route. No attacks were recorded in the past week in the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandab, with the last confirmed attack recorded on August 24. Following talks with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Berlin, the emir called for diplomatic efforts to de-escalate conflicts across the Middle East. On the sidelines of the visit, Qatari Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani met his German counterpart Johann Wadephul. items.title: Trump says US will find out about Iranian dirty bomb plot 'rumour'
items.summary: Trump says US will find out about Iranian dirty bomb plot 'rumour' US President Donald Trump said on Friday that there was a "rumour" that Iran was building a dirty bomb. He added that if Iran was doing so, the United States would find out and stop it. CNN had reported earlier this week that US intelligence indicated Iran could be attempting to build a dirty bomb and detonate it in Washington. Iran's foreign ministry denied the allegations on Tuesday, calling them "baseless". A dirty bomb is far less destructive than a nuclear bomb, which relies on a fission reaction. Speaking to reporters, Trump also repeated his claim that the US has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz. "Last week, we took out record amounts of oil from the Hormuz Strait. Our navy has a blockade," he said. "We have total control over the Hormuz Strait." "Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, ever," he added. Michael Kofman (Carnegie Endowment), Dara Massicot (Carnegie Endowment), and Amos Fox (Arizona State University) join Ryan to discuss. Over 115 strikes claimed by Iran or groups aligned with Tehran have damaged 26 military bases and other infrastructure belonging to the US across the Middle East, The Associated Press reported. The analysis, using satellite imagery, indicated that Iranian attacks on US sites in the region have mostly targeted early-warning systems, aircraft and buildings, resulting in billions of dollars’ worth of damage to US equipment. items.title: Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper hit in Houthi strike on Saudi wealth fund HQ
items.summary: By Timour Azhari RIYADH, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Riyadh's tallest skyscraper, headquarters of the Saudi sovereign wealth fund, was struck on Thursday by a suspected Houthi missile in the latest blow in the Iran-backed Yemeni group's war with the kingdom. The strike blew out windows across seven to eight floors of PIF Tower, bending parts of its metal facade. It was the second time in less than two weeks that a Houthi attack damaged a landmark in Riyadh's financial district, with state oil giant Aramco's building hit in a November 8 attack.

items.title: Trump says US will 'see what happens' in conflict with Iran after January 1
items.summary: Nov 19 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump said in comments broadcast on Thursday that the United States would "see what happens" in its conflict with Iran after January 1, without explaining what the significance of that date might be. In recent weeks, Trump has alternated between threats of escalation against Iran and indicating he could wind down hostilities, with the two sides in a standoff over efforts to resolve the conflict.

Iran has not granted the International Atomic Energy Agency access to those nuclear facilities since the military strikes against them in June 2025.

items.title: Trump says he will 'see what happens' with Iran after 1 January
items.summary: Trump says he will 'see what happens' with Iran after 1 January US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that Washington would "see what happens" as regards its war on Iran after 1 January. “We're going to have a new year coming up, and we'll see what happens after January 1. But they've been nasty,” Trump told Fox News during his trip to China. Trump made the comments during an interview in which he was asked about a CNN report that Iran was planning to detonate a “dirty bomb” in Washington. A dirty bomb uses conventional explosives to spread radioactive material. Trump downplayed such a threat, saying “I don't think so”, when asked if people in the capital should be alarmed.

items.title: China issues 'peace declaration' agreed with Trump and Putin
items.summary: China issues 'peace declaration' agreed with Trump and Putin China has released a “peace declaration” it said its President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin had agreed on at their unprecedented three-way meeting, where they said nuclear wars were futile and should never be fought. All three countries committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security, according to a four-point declaration published by Chinese official media Xinhua. The leaders reportedly discussed Russia's war in Ukraine and the US-Israeli war on Iran. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons, Xinhua said. The three heads of state also agreed on reform for a "more effective" United Nations, and said that the International Criminal Court and similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction, according to the declaration.

Door de oorlog konden er een deel van dit jaar geen olietankers meer door de Straat van Hormuz tussen Iran en Oman, terwijl juist door die zeestraat een groot deel van de olie uit het Midden-Oosten naar de rest van de wereld wordt geëxporteerd. Gigantische klap De afsluiting leidde tot torenhoge benzine- diesel- en kerosineprijzen. "De Hormuz-crisis gaf het energiesysteem een gigantische klap", zegt IEA-directeur Fatih Birol. "De energiesector en de wereldeconomie hebben dan wel weerbaarheid laten zien. Maar hoe langer de crisis duurt, hoe dieper deze zijn sporen nalaat. Ik zie geen geloofwaardige manier waarop de energiewereld teruggaat naar hoe het hiervoor was." Het agentschap doet niet één toekomstvoorspelling, maar schetst verschillende scenario's van hoe de energiewereld zich zal ontwikkelen. It is a historic moment in more ways than one, with the leaders of the world’s three most powerful countries around the same table. Ukraine, the war in Iran, nuclear disarmament and artificial intelligence are all expected to be discussed, and the summit has stoked fears of a carve-up of the world into spheres of influence. During an interview with Fox News, Trump said: "We don’t need any help. We’ve defeated their navy, we’ve defeated their air force, we’ve defeated their anti-aircraft." The comments come ahead of his expected  trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China. He also claimed that Tehran's missiles are "down to about 12, 13% of what they were, and they want to make a deal, so I don’t need help. I’m not going to go in asking for any help," adding that the US has "total control of the Hormuz Strait". "They want to make a deal, but I want a deal that can be lasting," the US president stressed. "I’m going to finish it off -- soon. I mean, one way or the other, we’ll finish it off."

items.title: Pentagon fails 9th straight audit, can't account for $2 trillion
items.summary: Taxpayer money is flowing to the Pentagon at record levels, yet the Pentagon can’t actually tell you where all that money is going. That’s the conclusion from the Pentagon’s 9th consecutive failed financial audit , which continues to leave the Pentagon as the only major federal Department to have never received a “clean” department-wide audit. Nonetheless, the Pentagon celebrated the audit results in a press release proclaiming that, “For the first time in Department history, clean audit opinions will cover more than 56 percent of DoW assets.” What isn’t mentioned in that press release is that the Pentagon has more than $4.8 trillion in assets, meaning that more than $2 trillion in assets do not have clean audits. items.title: Iran-backed Iraqi group refuses to withdraw from stronghold
items.summary: Iran-backed Iraqi group refuses to withdraw from stronghold Kataeb Hezbollah, Iraq's Iran-backed paramilitary group, said it will not leave its stronghold despite the US-backed prime minister calling on the armed faction to withdraw and allow the army to enter. On Monday, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi gave Kataeb Hezbollah an unspecified deadline to withdraw from Jurf al-Sakher, south of Baghdad, after the government earlier said an investigative committee had confirmed oil smuggling in the area - a claim the armed group denied. "I can state decisively and with absolute certainty that the dream they dream of the Kataeb withdrawing from Jurf al-Sakher will not come true, not even over our dead bodies," Abu Taleb al-Saidi, a Kataeb Hezbollah commander, told AFP during a press visit to the area. A security source told AFP that the deadline for Kataeb Hezbollah to withdraw from the area south of Baghdad was on Friday. Saidi stressed that his group did not want a confrontation with Iraqi armed forces.

items.title: Iran’s Ghalibaf warns US, Israel against targeting civilian infrastructure
items.summary: Iran’s Ghalibaf warns US, Israel against targeting civilian infrastructure Iran’s top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has warned of retaliation to the US and Israel after a New York Times report quoted analysts pointing to Tehran's "dual-use" of civilian infrastructure. "Prepping the next round on civilian infra, their 'experts' tell NYT: 'dams near Iran’s missile sites are dual-use.'," he mockingly referenced the article. "Cool. New rule: Any dam, port, or power plant near a US or Israeli base is dual-use. We’ll apply your logic consistently and even-handedly," Ghalibaf added. The US and Israel have previously attacked civilian areas and infrastructure across the region under the guise that they are used for military purpose, despite having no evidence for such claims. As a result, countless civilians have been killed and wounded in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.

items.title: US keeps punishing Iraq to get at Iran
items.summary: Washington’s latest attempt to restrict Iraq’s economic relations with Iran exposes a serious contradiction in the U.S. approach toward Baghdad. While Washington seeks to establish an expanded bilateral partnership following the withdrawal of its forces from Iraq, it continues to push Baghdad to become part of Washington’s confrontation with Tehran. This policy risks strengthening those political forces in Iraq that Washington seeks to weaken. On November 8, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein revealed that the U.S. Treasury had demanded the closure of all but two border crossings with Iran. This in turn followed Trump’s alleged threat to strike Iraqi armed factions if they participated in renewed fighting on behalf of Iran. items.title: Will Syria entry into Mecca pact mean clash with the Houthis?
items.summary: Syria appears likely to soon join the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, a collective defense agreement established several months ago by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan. This development would constitute a milestone in Damascus’ efforts to reassert itself within the region’s security architecture following Syria’s gruesome civil war. Membership in the pact could enhance the legitimacy and prestige of post-Assad Syria while bolstering its military capabilities and deepening partnerships with influential regional states. Syria could benefit from more intelligence cooperation, military training, and Saudi financial support. All this could complement Damascus’ existing security partnership with Ankara. But it’s not all milk and honey. Joining the security configuration could expose Syria to foreign conflicts and geopolitical rivalries while undermining Damascus’ ability to prioritize redevelopment at home.
